question: Is CPT code 93040 reimbursable when billed with split-bill modifiers 26 or TC?
answer: No. CPT code 93040 includes both the technical and professional components and is not reimbursable when billed with split-bill modifiers such as 26 or TC.

question: Which CPT codes represent the technical-only and professional-only components of a rhythm ECG with 1–3 leads?
answer: CPT code 93041 represents the technical component only, and CPT code 93042 represents the professional component only.

question: How many times per year may CPT code 93050 be reimbursed?
answer: CPT code 93050 may be reimbursed up to four times per year for any provider.

question: Can CPT codes 93306 and 93307 be reimbursed when billed on the same date of service for the same recipient?
answer: No. CPT codes 93306 and 93307 are not reimbursable when billed for the same recipient on the same date of service by any provider.

question: Under what conditions may multiple ECGs performed on the same date be separately reimbursed?
answer: Multiple ECGs may be separately reimbursed when performed at different times on the same date by the same provider and billed with modifier 76, with the number of ECGs entered in the units field of the claim.

question: Is CPT code 93225 reimbursable when billed with critical care codes 99291 or 99292?
answer: No. CPT code 93225 is not reimbursable when billed with critical care codes 99291 or 99292 by the same provider for the same recipient and date of service.

question: Is CPT code 93227 reimbursable when billed with critical care services, and are there documentation requirements?
answer: Yes. CPT code 93227 is reimbursable when billed with critical care codes 99291 or 99292 for the same recipient and date of service, provided justification is included in the Remarks or Additional Claim Information field of the claim.

question: What are the billing frequency limits for wearable mobile cardiovascular telemetry CPT codes 93228 and 93229?
answer: CPT codes 93228 and 93229 may be billed once per 30 days.

question: Under what circumstances is ambulatory blood pressure monitoring reimbursable without a TAR?
answer: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring is reimbursable without a TAR for outpatient patients with conditions such as suspected white coat hypertension, suspected masked hypertension, hypotensive symptoms while taking antihypertensive medications, or autonomic dysfunction, subject to a frequency limit of two times per year.

question: What are the authorization and documentation requirements for reimbursement of a wearable cardiac defibrillator under HCPCS code K0606?
answer: Reimbursement for HCPCS code K0606 requires an approved Treatment Authorization Request, is limited to one month at a time up to a maximum of three months, and reauthorization requires documentation of medical necessity, a face-to-face cardiology evaluation, and objective evidence showing use for more than 20 hours daily.

question: Are CPT codes 93000 through 93010 reimbursable when CPT code 93015 has already been paid for the same date of service?
answer: No. CPT codes 93000 through 93010 are not reimbursable when CPT code 93015 has already been paid to the same provider for the same recipient and date of service.

question: May CPT codes 93307 and 93350 be reimbursed when billed together for the same recipient on the same date of service?
answer: No. CPT codes 93307 and 93350 are mutually exclusive and are not reimbursable when billed together for the same recipient on the same date of service.

question: What billing options are allowed for CPT codes 93308, 93320, and 93321 when professional and technical components are involved?
answer: These codes may be reimbursed either as one professional component billed with modifier 26 plus one technical component billed with modifier TC on the same date of service, or as one professional component billed on different dates of service by the same professional provider.

question: Is Doppler echocardiography reimbursable without submission of a report?
answer: No. Claims for Doppler echocardiography must be billed with an appropriate ICD-10-CM diagnosis code and are reimbursable only if a report is submitted with the claim.

question: What training requirement must providers meet to bill echocardiographic procedure codes?
answer: Providers must have completed at least six months of dedicated training in an established echocardiographic laboratory to bill echocardiographic procedure codes.

question: What is the billing frequency limit for CPT codes 93293 and 93294 through 93296?
answer: CPT code 93293 and CPT codes 93294 through 93296 may be billed once per 90 days.

question: How frequently may CPT codes 93264, 93297, and 93298 be billed?
answer: CPT codes 93264, 93297, and 93298 may be billed once per 30 days.

question: What authorization requirement applies to comprehensive intracardiac electrophysiological evaluation CPT codes such as 93619 through 93622?
answer: Comprehensive intracardiac electrophysiological evaluation CPT codes require prior authorization, and a Treatment Authorization Request must be submitted for reimbursement.

question: What billing rule applies when multiple transesophageal echocardiography CPT codes 93312, 93315, and 93318 are billed on the same date of service?
answer: Only one of CPT codes 93312, 93315, or 93318 may be reimbursed on the same date of service, and subsequent claims must use the same procedure code with the appropriate modifier.

question: Which CPT codes for cardiac catheterization require a Treatment Authorization Request?
answer: Cardiac catheterization CPT codes 93451 through 93462 require a Treatment Authorization Request for reimbursement.
